data.about: Two equal and opposite forces at arm d form a force pair — a pure moment with no resultant. A movable reference line splits the moment into F_o·d_o + F_u·d_u, yet the sum stays F·d wherever the line lies; even below the pair, where the lower share counts negative, the total does not change.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: a horizontal force F₀ pointing right — its line of action is fixed
steps.title: The upper force F₀

steps.caption: an equal and opposite force Fᵤ below it: together they form a FORCE PAIR — the resultant is zero, what remains is pure rotation
steps.title: The lower force Fᵤ

steps.caption: the perpendicular distance between the two lines of action: d = 2 · distance (slider) — measured by the tall dimension column
steps.title: The arm d

steps.caption: the pair turns with moment M = F · d, here clockwise — the arc marks the positive sense
steps.title: The moment M = F · d

steps.caption: choose ANY horizontal reference line by sliding J on the dashed vertical (or use the buttons in the panel)
steps.title: A reference line through J

steps.caption: d₀ = distance from the line of action of F₀ down to the reference line
steps.title: The upper share d₀

steps.caption: dᵤ = distance from the reference line down to the line of action of Fᵤ
steps.title: The lower share dᵤ

steps.caption: each force contributes its lever about the reference line — and the sum is ALWAYS F·d: drag J, the split changes, the moment does not
steps.title: M = F₀·d₀ + Fᵤ·dᵤ

steps.caption: push J below the pair (button dᵤ = −1): the lower share turns negative, d₀ − dᵤ = d, and M stays F·d — a couple has the same moment about every point
steps.title: Independence of the reference
